title: Workflow for creating 3D characters?
author: JedahVoulThur
selftext:
Since the beginning of the current year (2024) I've been trying to find the perfect workflow for my use case.

I started the year by generating "character turnaround" of a consistent character from multiple perspectives. I accomplished it by using Wonder3D then aligning the images using GIMP and manually correcting any inconsistency, then upscaling through Krea.

Once accomplished I thought about sculpting a mesh using a Make Human model and some downloaded clothes that were close in design to the ones in the picture. Then using photographic projection, for the texture, some shading (I love NPR but you can go with photorealism if you prefer it) and then to animation... It all sounded very cool and I was doing it but it was a lot of work and I thought there should be a better way.

I tried two pages that had the option of "image to 3D" Charmed and Meshy. The second one impressed me the most, especially with the possibility to improve the textures after generation of the model. If I had the possibility to pay for its subscription, I'd do but sadly I live in a shitty third world country and can't afford it so I have to find another free way, and then I found Tripo3D.

That site blew my mind. It generates models really fast and it's very generous with the free credits (coff coff unlike Rodin coff) and the results are amazing.
There are defects, sometimes the clothes have holes and the hands look ugly as hell like it always is with AI generation. 
I recommend using a character in A-pose instead of T-pose to avoid the legs or feet to be joined together.
If you want a static object or a character that won't have a lot of animation, you won't need anything else. I recommend improving it a little in Blender though, simmetrize the end model, sculpt some details, improve the textures, retopologize, unwrap, etc 

But I'm a masochist that wants the character to have animated hair and clothes, and for that the best solution I've found is to use the generated model as just a base to then sculpt over it. I though about using the free Blender free human base mesh: https://www.blender.org/download/demo-files/#assets
and sculpt over it all the details or making it stick to the tripo model. 

But while reading this, I thought about a different idea. Making the character in A-pose and wearing only their underwear for the reference images and generation of the 3D model. Then symmetrize, sculpt over it to improve the features, use some downloaded hands to replace the generated ones, apply photographic projection, make the hair as a separate object, then generate models for the clothes, layer by layer and join them one by one to the model.

What do you think? What workflow do you use for generating 3D models? What software or website?

comments.author: JedahVoulThur
comments.body:
A year has passed after I posted this and the tools have improved a lot, and new ones have been released.
I not generate the concept character and turnaround using chatGPT, Krea and Seaart. I don't use Wonder3D anymore. 

For the image to 3D aspect, new tools like Trellis and Hunyuan3D have appeared and while they are fine (and free), Tripo is still the winner IMHO. It's current model version is 2.5 and it's amazing how much it has improved since the time my op. If I could pay for the prime version, I definitely would because it adds the option to use multiple perspective images for the generation and also it creates HD textures. But even the free version is decent enough, if you have the skill to manually fix details in Blender.

I'm excited for the future versions or new tools that might appear during this year, as everyone says "these are the worst versions we'll ever have".

replies.author: natandestroyer
replies.body: Hey, what do you use for 3D rigging and animation? Mixamo and Acurrig don't work for me

replies.author: JedahVoulThur
replies.body:
\> what do you use for 3D rigging and animation?

Blender with rigify for the rigging, and Cascadeur for animating. I recommend symmetrizing and retopologizing in Blender before rigging though.

\> Also, what do you think of Hunyuan 3D 2.5? It is giving me amazing results.

In my experience gave decent results. I now recommend sparc3D: https://lizhihao6.github.io/Sparc3D/. It blew my mind the levelof detail of the generation with this one, even thoug it doesn't generate textures it outputs the best models (they still need retopologizing for animation).
